prs.title: [Kernel] CUTLASS blockwise FP8 GEMM for SM89 (Ada) with per-token activation scales
prs.head: dbe22a894e66c11e03f47a70867c93b0c26bb410
prs.summary:
## Overview

Add a CUTLASS block-FP8 GEMM for SM89 (Ada: L4, L40S, RTX 4090, RTX 6000 Ada) that takes vLLM's block-quantized layout directly: per-token-group activation scales (1x128) and 128x128 weight scales. Today these GPUs have FP8 tensor cores but block-FP8 checkpoints (e.g. Qwen3-*-FP8, DeepSeek-style) run through Marlin weight-only. vLLM logs "Your GPU does not have native support for FP8 computation" on an L4. Closes the kernel part of #58241. Builds on the SM89 test enablement in #60171.

## Claims

- New SM89 kernel, adapted from CUTLASS's Ada blockwise FP8 example (example 94, which uses one activation scale per 128x128 block) to per-token activation scales. It uses Ada FP8 tensor cores (QMMA e4m3).
- `cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8` returns True on SM89 (CUDA >= 12.4), so `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` is selected instead of Marlin.
- On an L4, end to end on Qwen3-8B-FP8: ~1.42x throughput, ~1.33x faster at batch 32, ~3.6% slower at batch 1, gsm8k unchan

prs.title: [Kernel] Use 16-row tiles for SM89 int8 CUTLASS GEMM at M in (16, 64] when they don't add waves
prs.head: 8c897b571df5c61fced10d1c2838dd240d893a19
prs.summary:
## Overview

Fixes #56924. On SM89 (Ada), the int8 W8A8 CUTLASS GEMM gets ~1.5x slower when M goes from 16 to 17, and again from 32 to 33. The dispatch moves from 16-row tiles (`sm89_int8_config_M16`) to 32-row tiles at M=17 and 64-row tiles at M=33. For the small-N layers of models like Qwen3-1.7B (N=2048, K=2048) that halves or quarters the number of CTAs (32 CTAs with 32x64 tiles on a 128-SM RTX 4090), so most of the GPU sits idle and each CTA does more work.

This PR uses the existing `sm89_int8_config_M16` config for M in (16, 64] when its 16-row tiles fit in the same number of waves as the current config, or when the current config already needs two or more waves and the 16-row grid adds at most half again as many. The rule reads the SM count once per device. No new kernel configs, no new template instantiations beyond what M <= 16 already uses.
